name: Edge head-gradient direction readout from head difference between adjacent declared nodes, with refusal

statement.latest: \text{Let a canal graph have a declared edge } e=(u,v) \text{ between adjacent gauged nodes, with } \mathbb{Q}\text{-valued water-level readouts } h_u(t), h_v(t) \text{ on declared datums, each within a declared staleness window, and declared per-gauge resolutions } \varepsilon_u,\varepsilon_v>0.\quad \Delta_e(t) := h_u(t) - h_v(t).\quad \text{readout}(t) \text{ is evaluated as a total function, refusal rows checked BEFORE direction rows, in this fixed precedence:}\quad \boxed{\text{readout}(t) := \begin{cases} \text{REFUSED (UNDECLARED\_EDGE)} & e \text{ not a declared edge of the graph} \\ \text{REFUSED (MISSING\_INPUT / STALE\_INPUT)} & \text{else if } h_u(t) \text{ or } h_v(t) \text{ missing or outside its staleness window} \\ \text{REFUSED (DATUM\_MISMATCH)} & \text{else if } h_u, h_v \text{ declared on different datums} \\ \text{REFUSED (CONTROL\_STATE\_MISSING)} & \text{else if } e \text{ has a declared control structure whose state is missing or stale} \\ \text{REFUSED (CONTROLLED)} & \text{else if } e \text{'s declared control structure state is CLOSED or pumping} \\ u \to v & \text{else if } \Delta_e(t) > \varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v \\ v \to u & \text{else if } \Delta_e(t) < -(\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v) \\ \text{UNRESOLVED} & \text{else } (|\Delta_e(t)| \le \varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v) \end{cases}}
statement.note_ascii: For a declared edge e=(u,v) of a canal graph with Q-valued gauged water-level readouts h_u(t), h_v(t) on declared datums, each within a declared staleness window, and declared per-gauge resolutions epsilon_u, epsilon_v > 0: Delta_e(t) := h_u(t) - h_v(t) (a spatial retained difference between two adjacent nodes, in place of the temporal lag-k retained difference of PROP-FLOOD-01). readout(t) is a TOTAL function evaluated in this fixed precedence, refusal rows before direction rows: (1) UNDECLARED_EDGE if e is not a declared edge of the graph; else (2) MISSING_INPUT or STALE_INPUT if either h_u(t) or h_v(t) is missing or falls outside its declared staleness window; else (3) DATUM_MISMATCH if h_u and h_v are declared on different vertical datums; else (4) CONTROL_STATE_MISSING if e has a declared control structure (gate/pump) whose operational state is itself missing or stale; else (5) CONTROLLED if e's declared control structure state is CLOSED or actively pumping; else (6), only once none of (1)-(5) fire, the direction rows: u->v if Delta_e(t) > epsilon_u+epsilon_v, v->u if Delta_e(t) < -(epsilon_u+epsilon_v), otherwise UNRESOLVED (|Delta_e(t)| <= epsilon_u+epsilon_v). CONTROLLED and CONTROL_STATE_MISSING both emit NO direction at all -- REFUSED is a non-value, not a direction, and the structure's declared state is never used to assign a direction (a closed gate or an active pump can hold or reverse flow against the natural gradient, so the head-difference readout is simply refused, not overridden into a directional answer).

definitions.h_u, h_v: Q-valued gauged water-level readouts at nodes u and v respectively, each treated only as its finite sampled value at tick t -- never as a continuum signal
definitions.epsilon_u, epsilon_v: declared resolution constants > 0, one per gauge (u's own and v's own); MUST come from each gauge's own stated sensor resolution; if a source does not declare one for a gauge, that gauge's epsilon must be labelled INSTINCT (a narrative/judgment call), never silently VERIFIED/MEASURED. The two are summed (epsilon_u+epsilon_v) because Delta_e(t) differences two separately-resolved readings, one per gauge, not one gauge against itself
definitions.staleness window: a declared per-gauge maximum age for a reading to still count as current; a reading older than its declared window is STALE_INPUT, not silently treated as current
definitions.datum: the declared vertical reference level each gauge's reading is reported against; h_u and h_v must be declared on the SAME datum for Delta_e(t) to be meaningful -- a declared datum mismatch is DATUM_MISMATCH, never silently assumed equal
definitions.edge declaration source: the declared source establishing that e=(u,v) is an actual edge of the canal graph (e.g. OpenStreetMap canal/waterway data, or an official canal-network document); adjacency is itself a readout of that source, never assumed from geographic proximity alone -- an edge not backed by such a source is UNDECLARED_EDGE
definitions.control structure state: the declared operational state (e.g. OPEN, CLOSED, PUMPING) of a gate/pump structure on e, itself a readout from a declared source (an operator log, a SCADA/telemetry feed, or a manual declaration), carrying its own staleness; a structure whose declared state is missing or stale is CONTROL_STATE_MISSING, distinct from a structure whose state is known and is CLOSED/pumping (CONTROLLED)

recommended_use: Report readout(t) per declared edge per tick as one of {u->v, v->u, UNRESOLVED, REFUSED(reason)}; never infer a network-wide flow pattern by chaining several edges' direction readouts without separately checking each edge's own staleness/datum/control declarations, and never present readout(t) as a measured flow rate or volume.

parents.evidence: Delta_e(t) := h_u(t) - h_v(t) is a direct application of the workspace's own root primitive (a retained difference exists, delta_R = (a sharp b), Th_coqc per readout_genesis Part I 'THE ONE-LINE MASTER EQUATION') to two adjacent nodes' readouts at the same tick, replacing any implicit continuum spatial gradient (a limit over vanishing edge length) with a finite retained difference between two actually-gauged nodes.

PROP-FLOOD-01 registers Delta_k(t) := h(t) - h(t-k), a TEMPORAL retained difference (same node, two ticks) with an epsilon-resolution sign readout RISING/FALLING/FLAT plus a NO_READOUT refusal branch. This proposal is the SPATIAL sibling of the same forced move: same node-pair-plus-epsilon sign-readout machinery, but the two readouts being differenced are two adjacent NODES at the same tick (h_u(t), h_v(t)) rather than one node at two ticks (h(t), h(t-k)); the epsilon-sign-readout core (RISING/FALLING/FLAT relabelled here as u->v/v->u/UNRESOLVED) and the refusal discipline (NO_READOUT generalised here to six REFUSED reason codes: MISSING_INPUT, STALE_INPUT, DATUM_MISMATCH, UNDECLARED_EDGE, CONTROLLED, CONTROL_STATE_MISSING) are reused unchanged in form from PROP-FLOOD-01, not re-derived. NOTE ON TOKEN CLASH: PROP-FLOOD-02 uses the string 'UNRESOLVED' as one of ITS REFUSED reason codes (a REFUSED sub-reason, |Delta_k(t)|<=epsilon). Here, in PROP-FLOOD-04, UNRESOLVED is a first-class READOUT CLASS on the same footing as u->v and v->u -- a determinate output of the total function, not a REFUSED reason -- so the same token names two different things across the two sibling proposals; this is stated explicitly here precisely to avoid conflating them.

CAN-001 (weld/M.01.v1) forces, at tier Th_coqc, `L_R = D_W - W` on a finite causal graph (D_W = weighted degree matrix, W = the graph's weight/adjacency matrix) as the retained graph/operator of admissible transport (readout_genesis E00.7). Its row action on a state x is (L_R x)_u = sum_v W_uv (x_u - x_v): each edge (u,v) of the underlying graph contributes exactly one retained pairwise difference (x_u - x_v), weighted by W_uv. Delta_e(t) := h_u(t) - h_v(t) is precisely that single-edge difference term, taken as a readout in its own right (with a sign classification against a declared resolution) rather than summed into the full Laplacian operator; it borrows the graph structure and the edge-difference primitive from L_R without asserting or requiring the rest of the Laplacian stepper (D_W, the full sum over neighbours, or any dynamics forced from it). sign(W_uv (x_u - x_v)) = sign(x_u - x_v) holds only for W_uv > 0 (a positive edge weight); the head difference Delta_e(t) is a driving-gradient readout only -- L_R does not imply that water flows, and neither does this proposal's direction readout.

"`Adm = 1` ⇒ expand; `Adm = 0` ⇒ record the obstruction; `Adm = ⊥` ⇒ record it as **unresolved and do not guess**. `⊥` (unresolved, \"not yet known\") and `0` (obstructed, \"actively blocked\") are two different statuses, not one collapsed \"no\"" (READOUT_GENESIS_CORE.md, lines 3771 and 3775-3776)
genesis_compatibility.note: Delta_e(t) is a readout of the single off-diagonal edge term (x_u - x_v) that composes L_R = D_W - W on the finite causal graph; it instantiates the already-forced graph-Laplacian edge structure directly and needs no new Genesis gate. Gate 2's three-valued admissibility maps directly onto this proposal's own three-way split: UNRESOLVED (|Delta_e(t)|<=epsilon_u+epsilon_v, the retained difference cannot be distinguished from zero at the declared resolution) is the Genesis bottom/unresolved value ⊥ ('not yet known', do not guess); each determinate REFUSED reason (UNDECLARED_EDGE, MISSING_INPUT/STALE_INPUT, DATUM_MISMATCH, CONTROL_STATE_MISSING, CONTROLLED) is the Genesis obstructed value 0 ('actively blocked', a determinate reason the construction does not apply), never collapsed into ⊥. root-level caution D applies here exactly as it does to PROP-FLOOD-01: Delta_e(t) is a readout of two gauge readings on a declared graph, never a claim about the physical flood state or the true flow field itself -- and the graph's own edge set (adjacency) is itself a declared readout (from OSM or an official document), not a given.

claim_boundary: No hydrological/hydraulic flow model of any kind is asserted (no discharge/velocity estimate, no channel capacity, no rainfall-runoff). Validity is limited strictly to: readout(t) is a total function of (h_u(t), h_v(t), epsilon_u, epsilon_v, declared staleness windows, declared datums, declared edge set, declared control-structure state) computed on Q, refusal rows evaluated before direction rows in the fixed precedence UNDECLARED_EDGE > MISSING_INPUT/STALE_INPUT > DATUM_MISMATCH > CONTROL_STATE_MISSING/CONTROLLED > {u->v, v->u, UNRESOLVED} -- never a silently-dropped or fabricated case.
honest_caveats: Head difference indicates the driving hydraulic gradient between two gauged points, not a measured flow -- readout(t) is not a discharge, velocity, or volume readout, and a nonzero gradient does not by itself certify that water is actually moving; sign(W_uv(x_u-x_v))=sign(x_u-x_v) only for a positive edge weight W_uv>0, and L_R does not imply that water flows.

A pump or gate on the edge REFUSES the head-difference readout entirely -- it does not override it into a direction. CONTROLLED and CONTROL_STATE_MISSING both emit REFUSED with no direction at all; this is why the declared structure state is never used to assign u->v or v->u, and why a missing/stale control-state declaration (CONTROL_STATE_MISSING) is kept as its own reason, distinct from a known CLOSED/pumping state (CONTROLLED).

For a long edge with intermediate inflows/outflows (unmodelled local drainage, tributary canals) between the two gauged nodes u and v, the two-point head difference can disagree with the true local direction partway along the edge; this construction only ever certifies a direction readout between the two DECLARED gauge points, never along the edge's interior.

This is a per-tick spatial readout, not a flow model or a forecast: readout(t) at one tick carries no claim about readout(t+1), and chaining several edges' direction readouts into an inferred network-wide flow pattern is out of scope and not licensed by this proposal.

Graph adjacency (which node pairs count as a declared edge e=(u,v) at all) must itself come from a declared source (e.g. OpenStreetMap canal/waterway data, or an official canal-network document) and is itself a readout, carrying that source's own resolution and staleness -- UNDECLARED_EDGE exists precisely to refuse a direction readout on any pair not backed by such a declared source.

epsilon_u and epsilon_v (and the datum/staleness declarations) are shared in spirit with PROP-FLOOD-01 and inherit the same sourcing requirement (MEASURED/VERIFIED only if a source states them, else INSTINCT); the threshold is epsilon_u+epsilon_v (not a single shared epsilon), since Delta_e(t) differences two separately-resolved gauge readings at two different nodes, each carrying its own declared resolution.

UNRESOLVED here is a readout CLASS (a determinate output of the total function, mapped to Genesis's ⊥), not a REFUSED reason -- this is the opposite role the same token plays in the sibling proposal PROP-FLOOD-02, where 'UNRESOLVED' names one of the REFUSED reason codes; readers must not conflate the two uses across the two proposals.
Not yet implemented or tested against any real canal-network gauge data; this is a design-stage proposal.
